headword: {働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}
reading: はたらきかたかいかく

definitions.explanation: A broad Japanese government-led initiative launched around 2016–2019 to reform Japanese working practices — including capping overtime, encouraging paid-leave use, promoting remote work, and improving work–life balance. More generally, any movement or program aimed at changing how people work.

examples.japanese: {働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}を{進|すす}める。
{政府|せいふ}は{働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}を{推進|すいしん}している。
examples.english: The government is promoting work-style reform.

examples.japanese: {働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}によって{残業|ざんぎょう}{時間|じかん}が{減|へ}った。
examples.english: Thanks to work-style reform, overtime hours have decreased.

examples.japanese: {働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}の{一環|いっかん}として、{在宅勤務|ざいたくきんむ}が{認|みと}められた。
examples.english: As part of work-style reform, working from home was officially approved.

notes:
A political and social keyword in contemporary Japan, composed of {働|はたら}き{方|かた} (way of working) + {改革|かいかく} (reform). Originally a signature policy of the Abe government, formalized in the 2018 {働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}{関連|かんれん}{法|ほう} (Work Style Reform Related Laws), which took effect in 2019. The term has since broadened to refer to any effort to reshape how people work.

KEY GOALS:
- {長時間|ちょうじかん}{労働|ろうどう}の{是正|ぜせい}: correcting long working hours
- {有給|ゆうきゅう}{休暇|きゅうか}の{取得|しゅとく}{促進|そくしん}: encouraging use of paid leave
- {同一|どういつ}{労働|ろうどう}{同一|どういつ}{賃金|ちんぎん}: equal pay for equal work
- {多様|たよう}な{働|はたら}き{方|かた}の{推進|すいしん}: promoting diverse ways of working (including telework and flextime)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}を{進|すす}める: to promote work-style reform
- {働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}を{推進|すいしん}する: to push forward work-style reform
- {働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}{関連|かんれん}{法|ほう}: Work Style Reform Related Laws
- {働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}の{一環|いっかん}として: as part of work-style reform

RELATED WORDS:
- ワークライフバランス: work-life balance
- {長時間|ちょうじかん}{労働|ろうどう}: long working hours
- {有給|ゆうきゅう}{休暇|きゅうか}: paid leave
- テレワーク: telework, remote work

CULTURAL NOTE:
The term reflects a broad societal reckoning with Japan's notoriously long working hours and overwork-related deaths ({過労死|かろうし}). It is frequently invoked in news, corporate announcements, and HR materials.
